Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):
  - Acute diarrhea x 3 days; frequency 4–5/day; variable consistency (loose to watery).
  - Mild abdominal pain.
  - One episode of vomiting.
  - Possible mild fever (patient unsure).
  - Appetite reduced but maintaining oral intake; able to drink fluids.
  - No blood or mucus reported in stool.
  - No recent travel; no unusual foods reported.
  - History of asthma (patient states “had asthma”/“still have it”).
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):
  - Father: hypertension; died of bowel cancer at age 62.
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:
  - Patient reports using an inhaler for asthma but could not specify name.
  - “Lexapro” listed by patient when asked about inhaler name (conflict noted; Lexapro is typically an antidepressant, not an inhaler). Dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - No OTC medications taken for current symptoms.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:
  - Acute diarrhea care discussed: maintain hydration; consider oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte).
  - Dietary guidance: follow soft/bland diet; avoid dairy, meat, fish, eggs during acute phase; may use yogurt/probiotics; gradual reintroduction of boiled/mashed vegetables, then meats after 48 hours symptom-free.
  - Red flags: seek care if stool frequency increases to ≥6–8/day, signs of dehydration, presence of blood in stool, or symptoms persist beyond one week.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

- Internal conflicts or contradictions: Patient reported using an asthma inhaler but named “Lexapro” when asked for inhaler; Lexapro is typically an oral antidepressant (conflict noted). Patient denied blood in stool; one unclear statement “mostly it’s been dry and red” could not be confirmed.
